prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1428; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in the parking lot of a retail store. Insured vehicle reportedly backed into a parked sedan while exiting a space. Claimant reports minor property damage to rear bumper and a concussion-related complaint of headache and dizziness. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Initial contact made by phone; recorded statement offered and scheduled.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the insured. Insured states the lot was busy and visibility to the rear was partly blocked by a delivery van. Insured acknowledges contact with claimant's vehicle at low speed and accepts that liability is likely. Photos of both vehicles requested and received.

Entry 3: Claimant contacted to confirm medical status. Claimant reports headache, light sensitivity, and some trouble concentrating at work, and says a physician diagnosed a concussion. Claimant was advised that we can review medical records once a signed authorization is returned. Claimant indicated they have not yet retained an attorney and asked general questions about the claim process. Explained the difference between property damage and bodily injury coverage and offered to answer questions.

Entry 4: Medical authorization form sent to claimant by email and mail. Requested treatment records, imaging results, and any work absence documentation. Claimant stated they will return the forms within the week. Reminded claimant that they may seek independent advice at any time and that the adjuster cannot give legal advice.

Entry 5: Physical damage estimate received from the repair facility for claimant's vehicle and reviewed. Estimate appears reasonable for rear bumper replacement and paint blending. Bodily injury file remains open pending receipt of medical records and a treatment update. Diary set for follow-up with claimant in two weeks.
